key_insight: Brain2Vec learns reusable 3D brain MRI representations that improve brain-age prediction and support classification with frozen features.
clinical_relevance: The model could support research on structural brain MRI by reducing task-specific training demands, but clinical utility is not established in the abstract.
method: Self-supervised pretraining on 74,425 T1-weighted brain MRI scans pooled across studies.
Use pretrained weights for downstream fine-tuning or extract features with the model frozen.
Probe spatial localization and latent-feature effects on reconstructed anatomy.
evidence_signal: Pretrained initialization improved brain-age accuracy and convergence versus random initialization; frozen embeddings outperformed anatomical volumetric features on four of five classification tasks.
watch_item: Performance across clinical sites, scanners, and patient populations requires further validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
